name: Centauri wafer probe
notes: 1 g wafer (1 mm across) on a 2.94 m² sail at 0.34 g/m²: sail mass equal to payload, so 1.94 m across. Rebuilt as an assembly of a real part and the sail law, and measured in the Centauri lab (kosmo/static/centauri-lab.html). Needs 17.6 GW at the sail for 0.1 c in 600 s, which fits a 10 km aperture; it is the only class of the eight that closes. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 0 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 0 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri small satellite
notes: A 6U bus and dispenser (25 kg with its sail) on a 194 m sail. Measured peak laser 1.52 TW against the concept table's 175 GW; the beam would need a 16.7 km aperture and the station 2,326 km² of radiator, so this class does not close inside the buildability caps. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 1 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 1 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri instrument probe
notes: 150 kg bus with a 100 kg instrument on a 612 m sail. 501 GW at the sail, a 161 km aperture for 90 % coupling: the beam, not the power, is what fails. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 1 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 1 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri robotic lander
notes: 1 t lander structure with four legs and 1,000 kg of payload on a 1.94 km sail. 271 GW at the sail; the 1,194 mm clampband at the launch interface is rated at 8 t and carries 17 t, which the lab reports as a warning. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 3 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 3 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri crewed capsule
notes: A 4 m capsule, trunk and 12 t of cargo on a 6.12 km sail, 4 crew. 1.67 TW at the sail and a 386 km aperture: four metres of crew capsule pushed by a sail six kilometres across. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 10 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 10 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri crewed habitat
notes: Columbus-class laboratory, node, two array wings and two PVR radiators, with a cargo can, on a 19.4 km sail. 17.4 TW at the sail; the collector alone would be 16,115 km², above the 1,000 km² structure cap. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 37 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 37 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri colony seed
notes: Modules, machinery and cargo totalling 2 kt on a 61 km sail. 112 TW at the sail, a 58 km aperture and 62,164 km² of collector; the concept table claims 16 TW and does not price the beam. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 212 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 212 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri full colony
notes: A 1 g rotating habitat ring, 100 t modules and 18 kt of cargo on a 194 km sail. 668 TW at the sail against the table's 94 TW; 372,340 km² of collector is the binding failure, and the model is at true size, so the sail is the whole silhouette. Rebuilt with an axial sail mount: the film stands on a 23 m deployable mast, clear of the structure by 21 m (see CENTAURI-CAD-REVIEW.md).

name: Centauri crewed habitat, 1 g ring
aliases: crewed habitat with a spin ring
notes: v2 of the habitat: the v1 hull and sail with a 55.9 m spin ring at 4 rpm (1 g at the deck) for 24 crew -- 1 deck of 843 m2, 1 living and 0 working, 35 m2 per person. The ring adds 409 t of structure, so the vehicle measures 623 t against v1's 212 t; the sail is unchanged because the sail law sizes the film to the payload. The berth sits on the spin axis, on the despun side of the bearing. Modelled from the measured assembly and pinned in parts/fleet-versions.js (see CENTAURI-VERSIONS.md). Re-cut in the QA pass (CENTAURI-QA.md): spin-bearing: the ring now turns on the drum mid-plane and the PMA docks on the far face, aft, instead of berthing inside the node (CENTAURI-AUDIT.md).

name: Centauri wafer probe, pellet beam
aliases: wafer probe with a pellet beam
notes: v3 of the wafer: the same hull with the sail and mast off and a beamed pellet stream bolted through a 0 kg thrust frame to a rigid hardpoint where the mast root was. Beamed pellet propulsion (magnetised pellet accelerator, NASA NIAC pellet-beam study): momentum arrives as a pellet stream, so there is no sail to diffract and no onboard propellant. The a 0 m x 0 m tank at 0 kg/m3. At a 1:1 mass ratio (the pellet stream is the propellant and joins in flight) the ship measures 0.0000015 t and reaches 10 % c, a 43.7-year crossing of 4.37 ly. Modelled from the measured assembly and pinned in parts/fleet-versions.js (see CENTAURI-PROPULSION.md).

notes: v3 of the instrument: the same hull with the sail and mast off and a solar-electric ion (next-c class) bolted through a 50 kg thrust frame to a rigid hardpoint where the mast root was.
